add_comment.description: Post a comment on a Jira issue.
add_comment.name: add_comment

parameters.description: The key of the issue to comment on, such as PROJ-123.
parameters.name: issue_key

parameters.description: Text of the comment to post.
parameters.name: body

body.description: Comment text content that was posted to the issue

id.description: Comment ID (unique identifier for this comment)

create_issue.description: Create an issue in a Jira project, with a title and, if you like, a description, type, priority and assignee.
create_issue.name: create_issue

parameters.description: The project to create the issue in.
parameters.name: project_key

parameters.description: Longer description of the issue. Supports Jira's text formatting.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: The kind of issue, such as Task, Bug or Story. Leave blank for a Task.
parameters.name: issue_type

parameters.description: How urgent the issue is, such as High or Low.
parameters.name: priority

parameters.description: The person to assign the issue to.
parameters.name: assignee_account_id

id.description: Jira issue ID (internal numeric identifier). Use the key field instead for most operations

self.description: Jira API URL for this issue, for direct API calls

url.description: Link that opens the issue in Jira, for a message

get_issue_details.description: Look up a Jira issue's title and status.
get_issue_details.name: get_issue_details

parameters.description: The key of the issue to look up, such as PROJ-123.
parameters.name: issue_key

id.description: Jira issue ID (internal numeric identifier). Use the key field instead for most operations

status.description: Current workflow status of the issue. Contains name and id for identifying the issue's state in the project workflow

id.description: Status ID in Jira's workflow configuration.

name.description: Current status name (e.g., 'To Do', 'In Progress', 'Done'). Move an issue to a new status changes it.

summary.description: Issue title/summary text. This is the main heading displayed in Jira

list_projects.description: List the Jira projects your connected account can see.
list_projects.name: list_projects

projects.description: Array of Jira projects accessible to the authenticated user. Each project contains id, key, and name. Use the key field when creating issues

list_transitions.description: List the statuses a Jira issue can move to from the one it is in now, with the move that takes it to each.
list_transitions.display_name: List the statuses an issue can move to
list_transitions.display_str_template: List the statuses {issue_key} can move to.
list_transitions.name: list_transitions

parameters.description: The issue's key, such as PROJ-123.
parameters.name: issue_key

list_transitions.result_str_template: Listed the statuses the issue can move to.

transitions.description: The moves the issue can make from its current status, each with the status it leads to

id.description: The move's ID. Give it to Move an issue to a new status as its Move ID when two moves lead to the same status

name.description: The move's name, as Jira shows it

to.description: The status the issue will move to

search_issues.description: Find the Jira issues that match a search, written in JQL, Jira's search language.
search_issues.name: search_issues

parameters.description: Which issues to find, in JQL, Jira's search language. For example: project = PROJ AND status = 'In Progress'.
parameters.name: jql

parameters.description: The most issues to return, from 1 to 100. Leave blank for 10.
parameters.name: max_results

parameters.description: To get more results, enter the next page token returned by the previous search.
parameters.name: next_page_token

issues.description: Array of Jira issues matching the search query. Each issue contains id, key, summary, status, assignee, created, updated, due_date, priority and issue_type. Use the key to perform actions on specific issues

assignee.description: Who the issue is assigned to. Every field is an empty string when the issue is unassigned, so they are always safe to read

accountId.description: Account ID of the assignee. Pass it as assignee_account_id when creating an issue for the same person

displayName.description: Assignee's name as shown in Jira

emailAddress.description: Assignee's email address, to email them directly. Empty when they have hidden it in their Jira profile

created.description: When the issue was created, as a timestamp. Use it to work out how many days an issue has been open

due_date.description: The date the issue is due (2026-10-12), empty when it has none

due_date_display.description: The due date ready to read in a message (Oct 12, 2026), empty when it has none

priority.description: Priority name (e.g. 'High'), empty if the project has no priorities

status.description: Current workflow status of the issue

id.description: Status ID in Jira's workflow configuration

name.description: Status name as this project spells it (e.g., 'To Do', 'In Review', 'Done')

statusCategory.description: The broad category Jira files this status under

key.description: One of 'new', 'indeterminate', or 'done'. Use this, not the status name, to tell finished work from open work: every project names its statuses differently but they all map onto these three categories

updated.description: When the issue last changed, as a timestamp

url.description: Link that opens the issue in Jira

next_page_token.description: Cursor token for fetching the next page. Absent when there are no more results

transition_issue.description: Move a Jira issue to another status, such as In Progress or Done. The project's workflow decides which statuses it can move to from the one it is in now.
transition_issue.display_name: Move an issue to a new status
transition_issue.name: transition_issue

parameters.description: The issue's key, such as PROJ-123.
parameters.name: issue_key

parameters.description: The status to move the issue to, such as Done.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Only needed if two moves lead to the same status: the ID of the one to make, from List the statuses an issue can move to. Otherwise leave blank.
parameters.name: transition_id

transition_issue.result_str_template: Jira issue moved to its new status.

status.description: The status the issue moved to, as Jira spells it. Absent when the move was given by its ID alone

transition_id.description: The ID of the move Jira made

description: Create, move, comment on and find issues in your Jira projects.

jira_issue_status_changed_trigger.description: Runs each time an issue moves to another status in Jira, such as from In Progress to Done, with who moved it and when.

output.assignee: Who it is assigned to: displayName, emailAddress, accountId.
output.changed_by: Who moved it: displayName, emailAddress, accountId.
output.due_date: Its due date, if it has one.
output.issue_type: The issue type, such as Bug or Task.
output.key: The issue key, such as ENG-123.
output.project_key: The project's key, such as ENG.
output.reporter: Who reported it: displayName, emailAddress, accountId.
output.status: Its status, such as In Progress.
output.status_category: Its status category: To Do, In Progress or Done.

parameters.description: Only run for issues in this project. Leave blank for every project the account can see.
parameters.name: project

parameters.description: Only run when an issue moves into this status, such as Done. Leave blank to run for every move.
parameters.name: to_status

jira_new_issue_trigger.description: Runs when an issue is created in Jira.

output.assignee: Who it is assigned to: displayName, emailAddress, accountId.
output.due_date: Its due date, if it has one.
output.issue_type: The issue type, such as Bug or Task.
output.key: The issue key, such as ENG-123.
output.project_key: The project's key, such as ENG.
output.reporter: Who reported it: displayName, emailAddress, accountId.
output.status: Its status, such as In Progress.
output.status_category: Its status category: To Do, In Progress or Done.

parameters.description: Only run for issues in this project. Leave blank for every project the account can see.
parameters.name: project
